items.stem: A workload should run only on dedicated nodes while other pods stay off them. Which combination achieves this?

options.text: Taint the nodes and add a matching toleration to the workload
options.rationale: Correct: taints repel other pods while the tolerated workload can schedule.

options.text: Add more CPU limits to the workload
options.rationale: Limits cap usage but do not reserve nodes.
Manual deletion does not prevent rescheduling onto the nodes.

options.text: Expose the workload with a NodePort
options.rationale: NodePort is about networking, not node placement.

items.explanation: Correct: taints repel other pods while the tolerated workload can schedule.

items.stem: A ClusterIP service is unreachable from outside the cluster. Why?

options.text: ClusterIP is internal-only; external access needs NodePort, LoadBalancer or Ingress
options.rationale: Correct: ClusterIP is reachable only inside the cluster.
Storage is unrelated to service reachability.

options.text: ClusterIP only works with privileged pods
options.rationale: Privilege level does not govern service exposure.

options.text: ClusterIP needs a taint to function
options.rationale: Taints affect scheduling, not service reachability.

items.explanation: Correct: ClusterIP is reachable only inside the cluster.

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate first steps to diagnose a pod stuck in CrashLoopBackOff? (Select TWO)

options.text: Inspect the pod's logs for the failing container
options.rationale: Correct: logs usually reveal why the container exits.

options.text: Describe the pod to read its events
options.rationale: Correct: events surface scheduling, image and probe failures.
Deleting the node is disruptive and rarely the cause.
Elevating privileges does not diagnose a crash loop.

items.explanation: Correct: logs usually reveal why the container exits. Correct: events surface scheduling, image and probe failures.
